PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert.
RATIONALE: Avoids masking multiple failures and simplifies root-cause analysis.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if >1 distinct Act operations or multiple scenarios in one test.
DECISION RULES: The method contains two calls to tabelaHash0.insere(...) (two Act operations) -> rule 1 triggers non-compliance.
VERDICT: non-compliant because the test performs two separate insert operations in the same method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent and not share mutable state.
RATIONALE: Allows arbitrary execution order and parallel runs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables or have proper setup/teardown.
DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After present but the test uses only local variables and does not modify shared/static state.
VERDICT: compliant — the test uses only local variables and does not rely on external test order or shared mutable state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Provide tests for happy path and at least one error/exception scenario.
RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and handling of invalid inputs.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when there are tests for both successful and error paths (e.g., assertThrows or @Test(expected=...)).
DECISION RULES: Only a single happy-path style insert is present; no exception or invalid-input tests. With only successful operations present, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant — no test of error/exceptional flows present.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should include boundary inputs (empty, zero, negative, max, etc.).
RATIONALE: Boundaries often expose off-by-one or range errors.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for empty string, zero, -1, MAX_VALUE, etc.
DECISION RULES: The test inserts using an empty string key (""), which is a boundary case for string inputs -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant — the test exercises the empty-string boundary for the key parameter.

PRINCIPLE: Extract repeated setup and avoid duplication via helpers/constants.
RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and eases maintenance.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of helper methods or short tests without repetition counts as compliant.
DECISION RULES: The class has a single short test (<10 lines) with no evident duplicated blocks; thus considered modular enough for its size.
VERDICT: compliant — no duplicated blocks in this single short test; helper methods not necessary here.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small (<20 lines) with low cyclomatic complexity.
RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to reason about and less error-prone.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests are short and have no loops/complex conditionals.
DECISION RULES: The test is short (~6 lines) and contains no loops or conditionals -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties, not only superficial checks.
RATIONALE: Comprehensive assertions catch subtle faults.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when tests assert multiple properties or collection size and contents; non-compliant when assertions are missing or superficial.
DECISION RULES: The test contains no assertions at all (no verification of outcome) -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant due to lack of assertions verifying the effect of operations.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not be ignored or commented out; they must be kept active.
RATIONALE: Ignored or commented-out tests hide regressions.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test present.
DECISION RULES: No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out tests are present in the shown method/class -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should reference requirements (IDs or annotations) for traceability.
RATIONALE: Links tests to requirements for impact analysis when requirements change.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if annotations or Javadoc reference requirement IDs.
DECISION RULES: No @Story/@Requirement annotations nor Javadoc mentioning requirement IDs present -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant — no traceability information is present for the test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Performance and security tests are separate and explicit.
RATIONALE: Unit tests usually do not cover performance/security; explicit timing or auth tests required to be compliant.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant only if explicit performance (@Test(timeout=...) used as a performance assertion) or security tests present.
DECISION RULES: This is a unit-style test class; although @Test(timeout=4000) exists, it is not a performance measurement or security test. Therefore mark as not-applicable.
VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.
RATIONALE: Descriptive names make failures easier to understand.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if names follow methodName_scenario_expectedBehavior patterns; non-compliant if generic names like test1, test4.
DECISION RULES: The method name is 'test4', which is generic and does not describe intent -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant due to non-descriptive test name.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Auto-generated tests should be minimal and focused.
RATIONALE: Generated tests can be verbose and less maintainable; signs include generic names and generation comments.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant when there are auto-generated names (test0,test1) or comments like 'Generated by'.
DECISION RULES: The class and method names and the presence of EvoSuite runner and a generic method name (test4) indicate code generation -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant — signs of heavy test generation (EvoSuite/EvoRunner and generic test name) are present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should show deliberate design (Given-When-Then, coverage plans).
RATIONALE: Thoughtful design leads to better coverage and maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming are present or tests cover multiple scenario types.
DECISION RULES: The test appears minimal and ad-hoc (single short test, no BDD comments or multiple scenarios), so mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant — no evidence of test-first design or Given-When-Then structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify observable behavior via public APIs and avoid implementation details.
RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle and easier to maintain.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests call public methods only and do not use reflection or access private fields.
DECISION RULES: The test calls the public insere method and uses no reflection or private-field access -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include descriptive messages where useful.
RATIONALE: Clear, specific assertions make failures easier to diagnose.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions are specific (assertEquals/assertThat) and include messages; non-compliant if assertions are missing or only generic.
DECISION RULES: The test contains no assertions at all -> non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use minimal, meaningful comments that explain why, not what.
RATIONALE: Excessive comments or commented-out code degrade maintainability.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if commented-out code or >50% comments; compliant if minimal helpful comments or class-level Javadoc.
DECISION RULES: The class has a brief Javadoc and no commented-out test code; not overloaded with comments -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid non-deterministic sources (random, time, external dependencies) or mock them.
RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), external I/O without mocks.
DECISION RULES: The test uses fixed string and new Object(), no random/time/external dependencies found -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Tests should not modify shared state or leave resources uncleaned.
RATIONALE: Side effects create inter-test dependencies and flakiness.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if only local variables are used and no persistent resources are created without cleanup.
DECISION RULES: The test uses local variables and does not persist data or modify static variables; no cleanup needed -> compliant.
VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification:

RATIONALE: Enables running specific subsets (unit/integration/smoke) in CI.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category annotations present with meaningful labels.
DECISION RULES: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), which classifies the tests -> compliant.
